summary: Mobile SDK retry storms after HTTP/2 SETTINGS misnegotiation causing elevated 5xx in us-east
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the mobile SDK reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses (502/503) beginning 2026-03-13 09:15 UTC. Failures concentrated on long-polling/streaming endpoints and webhook-style callbacks from mobile clients.

Impact:
- NovaHealth (dedicated) experiencing degraded API availability for mobile users (~18% error rate on streaming endpoints for 30+ minutes).
- Broader error elevation observed in prod-us-east (~3% above baseline for 20 minutes).
- Several sessions observed repeated reconnects leading to user-visible delays and duplicated requests.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, dedicated customer pool for NovaHealth
- API gateway + HTTP/2 proxy -> serving runtime (GPU-backed)
- Mobile SDK v2.4.1 (iOS and Android builds)

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 09:12: config sweep rolled to edge (ingress) cluster: http2 proxy settings tightened (new SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS default).
- 09:15: first customer report; telemetry shows a spike in long-lived stream disconnects and immediate retry spikes from mobile clients.
- 09:18: Support alerted SRE; initial mitigation: rate-limit aggressive retries at edge for NovaHealth.
- 09:28: temporary reduction in 5xx but intermittent flares continued while clients retried.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Establish streaming session from mobile SDK v2.4.1 to /v1/chat/stream on prod-us-east.
2. Simultaneously reduce SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS on the proxy to force negotiation.
3. Client receives partial SETTINGS frame (observed in packet captures) and immediately triggers SDK-level reconnect loop.
4. Reconnect storm floods gateway, some upstream runtimes return 502/503 and occasionally close worker processes.

Relevant logs / traces (excerpts):
- apigw/http2-proxy: "ERR_HTTP2_FRAME_INVALID: SETTINGS payload truncated from client 10.2.1.45"
- proxy: "stream-reset: last-stream-id mismatch; closing connection"
- serving-runtime: "upstream: connection aborted by peer during frame decode"
- runtime-monitor: repeated watchdog restarts on GPU worker due to bursty reconnects (OOM false positives logged at 09:19)

Initial hypothesis:
- A config sweep reduced HTTP/2 concurrency settings at the proxy leading to SETTINGS frame size/format mismatch with older mobile SDK behavior. The SDK reacts by aggressively reconnecting (hedged retry behavior), amplifying load and producing a transient cascade of 5xx responses and upstream worker churn.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Applied targeted client-side retry dampening via a rate-limit rule at ingress for NovaHealth's tenant ID (09:18).
- Rolled back the SETTINGS change on the http2-proxy for prod-us-east edge (09:25).
- Increased keepalive timeout and allowed graceful draining to reduce reconnect storm.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported 18% error rate; gathered sample pcap and SDK logs; escalated to SRE.
SRE (Liam): Noted config sweep at 09:12; reproduced truncated SETTINGS in packet capture; priority mitigation: rate-limit client retry at edge.
Customer (NovaHealth Ops): Confirmed mobile app saw 'connection error' dialogs; will coordinate to ship SDK telemetry after our hotfix.
SRE (Liam): Rolled back http2 SETTINGS change at 09:25; observed gradual drop in 5xx, continuing to monitor for worker churn.
Support (Aisha): Opened temporary support token for NovaHealth to test patched mobile client with updated HTTP/2 handling.
Platform Eng (R. Chen): Suggested adding defensive parse tolerance and metrics to detect partial SETTINGS frames; raised infra PR for follow-up.
SRE (Liam): Observed one runtime worker restart cascade correlated with reconnect peak at 09:19; investigating watchdog coupling with reconnect rate.
investigation_notes: Packet captures show SETTINGS payloads truncated when middlebox applied new max_concurrent_streams enforcement.
Mobile SDK v2.4.1 uses an optimistic hedged-retry policy: on transport anomalies it spawns N reconnect attempts with backoff that can be very short on mobile networks.
Proxy returned STREAM_RESET and occasional 502 when encountering frames out-of-order during concurrent stream renegotiation.
Serving runtime logs show worker CPU spikes and increased GC pauses during reconnect floods leading to watchdog restarts; not a direct GPU OOM but a cascade due to thread saturation.
Correlation between config rollout time and initial spike supports the hypothesis that the SETTINGS change was the trigger rather than application code.
No evidence of malicious traffic; patterns align with benign client retry amplification.
root_cause: HTTP/2 SETTINGS concurrency enforcement rolled out at edge produced partial/invalid SETTINGS frames for existing mobile SDK clients; SDK hedged-retries amplified the traffic causing gateway overload and transient upstream runtime restarts.
resolution:
- Rolled back the http2 SETTINGS change on the prod-us-east http2-proxy; applied short-term ingress retry dampening for NovaHealth tenant.
- Implemented a temporary server-side tolerant parse for truncated SETTINGS to avoid immediate connection tear-down.
- Coordinated with NovaHealth to ship mobile SDK patch (v2.4.2) softening hedged-retry behavior and handling SETTINGS negotiation failures with exponential backoff.
- Added observability alerting for partial HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames and a dashboard to track SDK retry storms.
follow_up_actions: Infra: add canary gating for HTTP/2 SETTINGS changes and automated rollback on partial-frame error spike (Owner: R. Chen, due 2026-03-21)
SDK: publish v2.4.2 to mobile channels with retry backoff fixes and SETTINGS negotiation tolerance (Owner: NovaHealth SDK team / Redwood SDK liaison, due 2026-03-18)
SRE: tune watchdog sensitivity to avoid cascading worker restarts under short-lived reconnect spikes (Owner: Liam Porter, due 2026-03-20)
Support: notify affected customers and include guidance in the mobile SDK upgrade notes (Owner: Aisha Khan, due 2026-03-17)
